questions.question: What type of disease is asthma, and what is its primary effect on the body?
options: It is an infectious disease that causes joint inflammation.
It is a non-infectious disease that causes breathing difficulties.
It is an infectious disease that affects digestion.
It is a non-infectious disease that blocks blood flow to the kidneys.

questions.question: During an asthma attack, what happens to the breathing (bronchial) tubes?
options: They widen to let more air in.
They remain completely unchanged.
They narrow, making it harder to breathe.
They dissolve and reform later.

questions.question: Which of the following is a recognized risk factor for developing asthma?
options: Eating too much dietary fibre.
Having an allergy.
Regular hand washing.
Spending time in high-altitude clean air.

questions.question: What is a defining characteristic of an infectious disease?
options: It can only be inherited from parents.
It cannot be passed from one person to another.
It can be passed from one organism to another.
It is always caused by an unbalanced diet.

questions.question: Which statement is true regarding non-infectious diseases?
options: They are spread by coughing and sneezing.
They cannot be passed from one organism to another.
They are always caused by viruses.
They can be cured by taking a single dose of antibiotics.

questions.question: How do eating an unbalanced diet and not getting enough exercise affect health?
options: They decrease the chance of catching a common cold.
They increase the risk of developing lifestyle diseases.
They make the breathing tubes wider.
They prevent any genetic conditions from developing.

questions.question: Which of the following lifestyle habits is known to increase the risk of developing lifestyle diseases?
options: Doing regular aerobic exercise.
Drinking plenty of water daily.
Smoking, drinking alcohol and using drugs.
Eating a high-fibre balanced diet.

questions.question: What are medicines?
options: Any illegal substances used for recreation.
Drugs that people take when they are ill.
Chemicals used only to make food taste better.
Solvents used for household cleaning.

questions.question: Into which two broad categories can recreational drugs be classified based on their general effects on the nervous system?
options: Antibiotics and pain relief.
Legal and natural.
Depressants and stimulants.
Solvents and inhalants.

questions.question: How do depressants affect a person's nervous system?
options: They speed up thoughts and improve reaction speeds.
They slow down thinking and reaction times.
They increase physical strength and coordination.
They have no effect on brain activity.

questions.question: What type of drug is alcohol, and what are the long-term risks of using it?
options: It is a legal stimulant that damages the lungs.
It is a legal depressant that can damage the brain and liver over time.
It is an illegal depressant that has no long-term health risks.
It is a medicine used to treat bacterial infections.

questions.question: What is a typical effect of a stimulant on the human body?
options: It makes you feel sleepy and slows down reactions.
It reduces your heart rate and numbs pain.
It makes you feel more alert and can give you quicker thinking and reaction times.
It causes immediate loss of consciousness and permanent memory loss.

questions.question: What substance is found in tobacco leaves that makes smoking highly addictive?
options: Tar
Carbon monoxide
Nicotine
Caffeine

questions.question: What is solvent abuse?
options: Swallowing prescription medications with water.
Inhaling chemicals from substances like glue or paint thinner to become intoxicated.
Injecting recreational drugs into blood vessels.
Overusing household cleaning liquids on kitchen surfaces.

questions.question: What are the potential consequences of solvent abuse?
options: Only minor temporary coughs with no long-term effects.
Improved concentration and respiratory health.
Risks of long-term health problems and it can lead to death.
Complete immunity to bacterial infections.

questions.question: In what way is vaping similar to traditional smoking?
options: It involves burning tobacco leaves directly in the mouth.
It involves consuming nicotine, which is detrimental to health.
It produces identical yellow ash and tar stains.
It has been proven to be completely harmless to the lungs.

questions.question: What is currently true about the long-term health effects of vaping?
options: They are fully known and documented to be completely safe.
They are identical in every way to the effects of drinking alcohol.
They are not yet fully known.
They are proven to prevent asthma attacks.
